hook: Nils Nilsson earned his PhD in electrical engineering from Stanford in 1958, then served in the United States Air Force before joining SRI International, where he spent 23 years building foundational tools for artificial intelligence. At SRI he co-invented the A* search algorithm and the STRIPS automated planning system, and co-directed Shakey, one of the first mobile robots able to perceive its surroundings, plan, and act. He returned to Stanford in 1985 and chaired its Computer Science Department until 1990, later becoming the Kumagai Professor of Engineering, Emeritus. Nilsson wrote nine books on artificial intelligence, including the 2010 history The Quest for Artificial Intelligence, and served as president of AAAI. He died in 2019 in Medford, Oregon, at age 86.

quick_facts: Co-invented the A* search algorithm (1968) with Peter Hart and Bertram Raphael, still a standard method for optimal pathfinding.
Co-developed STRIPS, one of the first automated planning systems, with Richard Fikes at SRI International in 1971.
Co-directed development of Shakey, among the first mobile robots able to perceive its environment and plan its own actions.
Chaired Stanford University's Computer Science Department from 1985 to 1990.
Authored nine books on artificial intelligence, including The Quest for Artificial Intelligence (2010).
Served as president of AAAI and received the IEEE Neural-Network Pioneer Award and the AAAI Distinguished Service Award.

achievements.title: A* search algorithm
achievements.impact: Co-invented with Peter Hart and Bertram Raphael at SRI, A* became the standard algorithm for finding optimal paths and remains foundational across robotics, video games, and networking.

achievements.title: STRIPS automated planning system
achievements.impact: Co-developed with Richard Fikes at SRI, STRIPS was one of the earliest automated planning systems and established representations still used in AI planning research.

achievements.title: Shakey the robot
achievements.impact: Co-directed development of Shakey at SRI, among the first mobile robots able to integrate perception, planning, and action, influencing decades of robotics research.

achievements.title: The Quest for Artificial Intelligence (2010)
achievements.impact: Wrote a widely used history of ideas and achievements across the field of artificial intelligence.

achievements.title: Stanford Computer Science Department chair
achievements.impact: Led the department from 1985 to 1990 after returning from SRI, shaping its research direction.
